items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: It was called the Ray Price Quartet. Ray Price was a banjo player.

ctx.x: Was there a role model for you about a musician who felt that, okay, I have to leave New Zealand, I have to take these stepping stones to get where I want to get.

I think it was a logical progression. I was always setting myself up against people, and ranking myself. Where do I fit within the scene? And after I’d pretty much played with everybody that I admired and I realized I was being accepted by these folks, then I would run into players from other countries who would come in, and a bunch of guys from Australia had said, “you should come to Sydney,” you know, “things will really happen for you.” So after hearing this enough times, when I was 21 I said okay.
